messages:
anna: Starting thread for ArgoHealth POC perf validation. They want concrete evidence on microburst recovery and token-level cost. Need run matrix + security checklist by EOD Tue.

raj: Proposed matrix: A) Ramp/Soak: ramp to 3k qps over 10m, hold 2h. B) Burst: 15k qps for 15s x8 with 30s spacing. C) Degraded case: route 25% to smaller model and measure failover latency. Capture p50/p95/p99 tokens, model queue time, and batch size.

liz: For context lengths, Argo says typical prompts 30 tokens (70%) and long 180 tokens (30%). They also do occasional tool-call walks (~5% of requests). We'll simulate that.

dustin: Ops notes: warm caches for 25m before any burst. Use continuous batching + max_batch_ms=12 to mimic production. For Dedicated, set node isolation tag so shards don't move. Also add per-request metadata to trace model_variant and route.

anna: Quick smoke commands (adapt for fortio/k6):
```
# mixed workload smoke
python infra/loadgen.py --mix "short:70,long:30" --prompt-len 30 --resp-len 45 --qps 3000 --duration 120m --tag argohealth-poc --out results/smoke.json
# burst test
python infra/loadgen.py --burst-qps 15000 --burst-duration 15 --bursts 8 --warmup 25m --out results/burst.json
```

raj: Metric checklist: token latency (server-side), end-to-end latency (includes tool-call overhead), GPU util, enqueue_wait_ms, avg_batch, request_failures, and any KMS latencies. If p99 token latency > 500ms during burst, capture stack traces and lower burst or route.

sec-bot: Uploaded ArgoHealth sec questionnaire v3: https://redwood-internal/sq/901 — they require BYOK for production and audit log extracts for each test. POC needs IP allowlist + signed NDA.

liz: Argo is OK with BYOK for POC if we can do ephemeral key caching. They explicitly asked whether KMS roundtrips will impact tail latency.

dustin: Yes — KMS API calls are ~6-10ms; with caching of derived keys on-host we avoid per-request KMS. For the POC we'll enable key cache with 30s TTL and surface in the sec answers. Document tradeoff: caching reduces latency but increases memory/attestation surface.

anna: Cost sketch request from Argo: give per-10k-token hosted vs dedicated. Use conservative defaults.

raj: From last bench: hosted ~ $0.030 / 10k tokens under burst patterns. Dedicated reserved ~ $0.015 / 10k tokens if steady baseline retained. If they use a lot of burst-minutes, add burst surcharge. I'll produce a simple calc by Wed.

anna: Argo also asked about failure mode during a sustained overload — what do we show them?

dustin: We'll demonstrate graceful degradation: route new requests to a smaller model (latency vs quality), and show autoscale cooldown behavior. Include a canary failover run in test matrix.

liz: Ops-bot FYI: reserving a Dedicated slot for Tue 09:30 UTC. ops-bot:reservation_id=dh-res-77821

ops-bot: Reservation dh-res-77821 created for 2027-02-10T09:30Z, pool=dedicated-standard-8.

anna: Next steps: Raj to post runbook + exact cost calc by Tue noon. Dustin to finalize warmup and caching config. Liz to answer sec questionnaire items 2.1-2.5 and confirm NDA. We'll do a coordinated smoke + burst Tue 10:00 UTC. If anything blocks, tag @anna. :calendar: 

raj: Aiming to include dashboard links (token-latency heatmap, batch-size violin, failure trace) in the runbook. Tagging all tests with `argohealth-poc` for filtering.

anna: Thanks all — closing thread for now. Will open a new thread for results writeup after run. :white_check_mark:
